# Who Was Worth the Pick?

I wanted to find out which fantasy football players **delivered the most value** in last season’s draft. Using data from ESPN’s Fantasy API and draft results from my league, I analyzed who truly lived up to their draft slot – and who didn’t.

---

## How I Got the Data

I pulled the full draft order, fantasy points scored across the season, and positional ranks for every drafted player. Using that, I calculated a custom version of **Value Over Replacement Player (VORP)** based on our league format:

- 14 teams
- 2 RB, 2 WR, 1 TE, 1 Flex (WR/RB/TE), 1 QB, 1 Kicker, 1 D/ST

VORP was calculated by comparing each drafted player’s points to the **average performance of a replacement-level starter at that position.**

---

## Draft Value Heatmap

The interactive plot below shows draft **round and pick number**, colored by the **VORP** of the player selected. **Hover over a cell** to view the player's name, position, average points, and draft position.

```{python}
import plotly.express as px
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
%config InlineBackend.figure_formats = ['svg']
heatmap_df = pd.read_csv("../data/raw/heatmap_df.csv")

# Step 1: Add hover text column to the dataframe
heatmap_df["hover_text"] = heatmap_df.apply(
    lambda row: f"<b>{row['player_name']}</b><br>"
                f"Position: {row['position']}<br>"
                f"Pick: Round {int(row['roundId'])}, Pick {int(row['roundPickNumber'])}<br>"
                f"VORP: {row['vorp']:.2f}",
    axis=1
)

# Step 2: Pivot VORP data
heatmap = heatmap_df.pivot_table(
    index="roundId",
    columns="roundPickNumber",
    values="vorp",
    aggfunc="mean"
)

# Step 3: Pivot hover text to match shape
hover_matrix = heatmap_df.pivot_table(
    index="roundId",
    columns="roundPickNumber",
    values="hover_text",
    aggfunc="first"
)

# Step 4: Plot with Plotly
fig = go.Figure(
    data=go.Heatmap(
        z=heatmap.values,
        x=heatmap.columns,
        y=heatmap.index,
        text=hover_matrix.values,
        hoverinfo="text",
        colorscale="RdYlGn",
        colorbar=dict(title="VORP"),
        showscale=True
    )
)

# Step 5: Clean layout
fig.update_layout(
    title="Interactive Draft VORP Heatmap",
    xaxis_title="Pick in Round",
    yaxis_title="Draft Round",
    yaxis=dict(autorange="reversed", tickmode="linear", dtick=1),
    font=dict(family="Arial", size=14),
    plot_bgcolor="white",
    margin=dict(t=60, b=40, l=60, r=40)
)

fig.show()
```

---

## Top Draft Steals

The table below highlights the **top 10 players** with the highest VORP in the draft. These were the most valuable picks relative to replacement-level players at their position.

```{python}
top_steals = heatmap_df.sort_values("vorp", ascending=False).head(10)
top_steals[['player_name', 'position', 'avg_points', 'vorp', 'overallPickNumber']].style.format({
    'avg_points': '{:.2f}',
    'vorp': '{:.2f}'
}).set_caption("Top 10 Draft Steals by VORP")
```

---

## Overdrafted Players

These players were selected early but returned **below-replacement performance**. In other words, they cost more than they delivered.

```{python}
undervalues = heatmap_df.sort_values("vorp").head(10)
undervalues[['player_name', 'position', 'avg_points', 'vorp', 'overallPickNumber']].style.format({
    'avg_points': '{:.2f}',
    'vorp': '{:.2f}'
}).set_caption("Most Overdrafted Players by VORP")
```

---

## Conclusion

This analysis reveals that fantasy value isn’t just about total points. **Drafting players who outperform their positional average** can give your team a serious edge.

Key Takeaways:
- Late-round hits can carry your team
- Don’t overpay for names without checking upside
- VORP helps normalize performance across positions

This kind of analysis can make you a smarter fantasy drafter next season.
